correctness.rationale: The radial beta integral gives m_j=j!/(beta)_j. Expanding the square of the quadratic leaves only one phase-sensitive term, 4m_2 Re(b^2 conjugate(ac)); independent signs average it out and a flip of exactly one of the outer modes reverses it. For fixed magnitudes, the maximal ratio uses maximal destructive interference in the input. With v=|b|^2, x=|ac|/v and t=|a|/|c|, minimizing H/(4m_2 v^2 x) in x is the strict equality case for m_2/x+x(t^2+4m_2+m_4/t^2). The balancing substitution for t then gives the displayed F_beta. The norm term in F_beta is convex by the vector-norm second derivative: its Cauchy–Schwarz residual is nonnegative and its vector dotted with its second derivative is positive. The cosh term gives strict convexity and uniform coercivity. A_beta-B_beta has sign beta-1, so the derivative at zero is positive and the unique minimizer is negative. Each of the three parameters increases strictly, which increases the minimum by comparison at the new minimizer. Uniform coercivity and local uniform convergence justify both limits of the minima; the scale change gives limiting moments j!. Sharp equality requires all three coefficients, the unique x,t, and the specified phase; constructive and destructive phases give opposite sides of the Rademacher comparison. An independent 65-digit decimal bisection in y=exp(s), /tmp/opencode/frozen-quadratic-endpoints.py, reproduced the illustrative endpoint and area-weight decimals. The proof, not the numerical check, gives the all-weight result.
residual_risks: Exact statements use the variational constants, not decimal rounding; no larger degree or infinite-dimensional space is covered.
